feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 1 (wheel_track 0.10, score 114.4) gave oval progress 0.47, oval oscillation 0.28 and max_error 0.061 to 0.066 m. Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.11, same controller) gave oval oscillation 0.259, line-loss 0.25, but oval progress 0.416 and s-bend progress 0.236, so the wider track cost progress. Iteration 4 showed that a lighter, more responsive drivetrain raised oscillation to 0.33 without a progress gain. Sensor lead and footprint tests (iterations 2, 3, 5, 6) all scored below iteration 1, so the 5-sensor, 12 mm, 0.03 m-lead layout should be kept. Integration point: the controller is unchanged (kp 2.5, kd 0.30, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction), and a narrower track raises turn rate per wheel differential by about 11 percent, so the effective gain is higher than in iteration 1. I did not retune kp, so that the wheel_track effect can be read cleanly. Change the next design by what the race shows. If oval progress is at or above 0.47 and oscillation stays at or below about 0.28, the narrower track is a gain, so try mass 0.7 kg to damp bend overshoot. If oscillation rises above about 0.3 while progress rises, the extra gain is causing jitter, so return to 0.10 m and use damping instead. If progress falls below 0.44 on the oval, the optimum is near 0.10 m, and further gains must come from the controller.
requested_changes: If oval progress is at or above 0.47 and steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.28 at wheel_track 0.09 m, but max_error is still at or above 0.06 m, set mass to 0.7 kg (from 0.6). Iteration 1 showed max_error of 0.064 to 0.066 m with small rms_error, so the excursion looks like bend overshoot that more yaw inertia should damp.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 at wheel_track 0.09 m while progress does not improve, return to wheel_track 0.10 m. Iteration 7 showed that the 0.11 m track cut oscillation from 0.282 to 0.259, so the 0.10 m setting is the measured balance point.
Keep the five-sensor 12 mm layout at y 0.03 m (x -0.05 to +0.05). Iteration 5 (lead 0.02 m) scored 91.8 and iteration 6 (lead 0.04 m) scored 109.9, both below iteration 1 (114.4).
